subject: Implementation sprint plan & POC success criteria — Optima Retail
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@optima-retail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation sprint plan & POC success criteria — Optima Retail

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on goals. Per our discussion, here's a concise recap and the proposed two-week POC implementation sprint so your team can evaluate Redwood in a production-like flow. Please flag anything missing.

Goal (what Optima needs to validate)
- Accurate product-category extraction and relevance for merchandising prompts (~95% P1 accuracy on your evaluation set)
- End-to-end latency under 250ms median for single-turn queries, p95 under 600ms for typical request sizes
- Throughput: sustain 30 QPS on the representative workload profile we discussed
- Integration: SDK-based streaming responses for long-form descriptions and tool-calling for price lookups

POC timeline & milestones (2 weeks)
- Day 0 (Oct 19): Dedicated trial environment provisioned (Redwood) + Optima access
- Days 1–3: SDK integration & test harness (Optima engineers) — we provide SDK snippets and a postman collection
- Days 4–8: Data model alignment & evaluation set run (joint) — we'll run batch evals and share concrete metrics
- Days 9–12: Latency/load tests + tuning (Redwood to advise batching/quantization settings)
- Day 14 (Oct 30): Final review, metric signoff, and next-steps (rollout or extended pilot)

Ownership
- Optima: devs integrate SDK routes, run local verification, share evaluation set and a short fail-case list
- Redwood: provision trial infra, provide SDK examples and a streaming demo, run backend perf tests, and share monitoring dashboard access

Integration notes (high level)
- Preferred path: Redwood SDK for Node/Python with streaming (server-sent events) for product descriptions; fallback to REST streaming if you cannot use the SDK initially
- Tool calling: we'll expose a secure tool-calling endpoint to perform price lookups and inventory checks; we recommend using the sandbox credentials during POC
- Authentication: API keys for the trial; if you need VPC/private deployment, we can propose a Dedicated trial (separate discussion)

Attachments I am including: optima_poc_plan_v1.pdf (detailed plan), redwood_sdk_snippets.zip (examples), sample_payloads.json (payload shapes + example responses).

Next steps / asks for Optima
1) Confirm owners and dev availability for Oct 19 kickoff
2) Share a small evaluation set (50–100 representative queries) and a prioritized list of success/failure cases by Oct 18
3) Confirm if you prefer Node or Python SDK first

I’ll set up a calendar invite for Oct 19 kickoff once you confirm.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation sprint plan & POC success criteria — Optima Retail

Thanks Monica — solid plan. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Owners: Priya (project lead) and I will own the integration work. We can allocate two devs (Amit and Lena) starting Oct 19.
2) SDK flavor: Node first (our backend microservice stack is Node). Please surface any non-blocking Python examples too.
3) Eval set: we'll share 80 queries by COB Oct 18; they will include multi-turn product context. Expect some longer-form responses (hence streaming is important).
4) Security: can you confirm data retention for the trial environment and whether logs will contain any customer PII? We need a short security statement to share with our InfoSec.

Also, can Jordan drop a quick example of the streaming route and a sample tool-calling flow so Amit’s team can get started?

If all looks good we’ll confirm owners formally and accept the Oct 19 kickoff.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
Optima Retail

Confirmed: Oct 19 kickoff, Node SDK, owners: Amit (integration), Lena (tests), Priya (project lead). We’ll share the 80-query eval set by COB Oct 18 as requested.

Security follow-up: Priya will share an InfoSec questionnaire with specific PII fields to redact. Jordan — can you confirm whether redaction is a manual mapping we provide or if Redwood can auto-scan typical PII (emails, phone numbers) during the trial? We prefer auto-scan + manual mapping for edge cases.

We accept the trial environment with the 30-day logs default, but would like the option to shorten retention if needed. Also please send a short checklist of the two sandbox endpoints (streaming + tool callback) and example curl commands so Amit can spin up a PoC service on Oct 19 morning.

I’ll expect the calendar invite shortly. Looking forward to the kickoff.
